intro.heads_up: Quick heads-up before we dive in: by the time this episode drops Tuesday morning, Blizzard's first round of Forever class tuning is scheduled to land that same day, and the Pouch of Violet Dust Twitch drop runs through Thursday, November 12.
rundown: Blizzard calling WoW: Forever the biggest launch in WoW history
a launch week of empty cities, lost zeppelins and Blizzard's fixes
Forever's first hotfix list, including a fresh pot of coffee for Kerlonian
Blizzard throwing out Classic power budgets, and the first class tuning pass
mega-raids and proximity voice from the Forever tech podcast
the community showing up, from a walk to 60 to a launch-week Twitch drop
gamepad support, Taldramir and the rest of Forever's extras
a big round of Venomous Abyss nerfs over on retail
and we'll close out the news with a faster, simpler Xbox app on PC

items.title: Blizzard: Biggest Launch in WoW History
items.synopsis: Blizzard's own accounts are calling Forever the biggest launch in WoW history, and the most returning players the game has ever seen.
points: Forever going live in every region at once, November 4 at 3 p.m. PST
the official World of Warcraft account posting "you made HISTORY" two days later
the biggest launch in WoW history by peak concurrent players, in Blizzard's own words
and the highest number of returning players in WoW history on top of it

points.text: no actual concurrent number attached, just the record claim
points.sub: Windows Central reported it as beating Wrath of the Lich King, from that same post

points: @Warcraft slapping the roof of Forever: 3,924 virtual machines, 251,136 GB of memory, 70,480 CPU cores
Blizzard ANZ showing heroes entering Azeroth one dot at a time, blue and red dots lighting up the world map

points.text: Twitch reportedly peaking around 1.12 million viewers, close to Classic in 2019
points.sub: that number is from X chatter, not from Blizzard

points: Mitch Jones, Sodapoppin and NmpLul reportedly running multi-day streams with $1 million in giveaways
Windows Central already asking whether retail is cooked
questions: From where you were standing on launch night, did it feel like the biggest launch ever?
Is Forever pulling players away from retail, or bringing back people who'd already left?

items.title: Empty Cities, Lost Zeppelins: Launch Week Fixes
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, Blue Posts
items.synopsis: Launch week was smoother than most, and Blizzard was on the forums answering the stuff that did break.
points: a player asking why they only see maybe 8 people inside the main city

points.text: Aggrend: some areas "not feeling as populated as they should," with numbers tweaked the next day
points.sub: that's layering; the read on X was that it started out too aggressive

points: boats and zeppelins getting "lost in the maelstrom" for extended periods
Blizzard spawning temporary portals at the docks and inside the zeppelin towers until the real fix landed
Invite-a-Friend players locked out of chat, guilds, parties, trading and leveling past 10, hotfixed launch night
PvP vendors temporarily unavailable in Orgrimmar, Stormwind and Dalaran on the Known Issues list
Vorsha the Lasher in Ashenvale disabled over a crash bug
group phasing still a problem from beta, with Kaivax walking players through the Refresh Now prompt

points.text: Horde PvP character creation reportedly throttled for faction balance
points.sub: from X chatter; we didn't find a Blizzard post on it

points: Blizzard's new bug report forum rules: "We read every single post" but can't reply to most
questions: Did either of you get stuck on a dock, in an empty layer, or behind a phasing wall?
Is a launch with this many players and this few problems the new bar Blizzard has to hit?

items.title: Forever's First Hotfix List
items.synopsis: Forever's November 6 hotfixes clean up the leveling road, and Blizzard had some fun writing them.
points: Blizzard brewing a fresh pot of Darnassus's finest coffee for Kerlonian Evershade

points.text: so he falls asleep less often during "The Sleeper Has Awakened"
points.sub: and you now start the quest with the Horn of Awakening to wake him up

points: "Vorsha the Lasher" no longer rudely lashing everyone in the zone
the Tanning Rack requirement lowered to 125 (was 140) so it stops blocking Leatherworking patterns
Zaetar's Spirit spawning again after Princess Theradras in Maraudon
creatures in Blackmaw Hold and The Drowned City no longer disengaging, and the Drowned City portal fixed
the troggs in Grol'bolar Quarry no longer respawning too quickly
Lasher Sproutlings, Blooming Lashers and Wrathvine in Teldrassil no longer immune to nature damage
Voidwalker base health going up by about 40 at all levels
Mages no longer learning a Research spell that shouldn't exist and losing it on relog
questions: Which leveling quest has been the biggest pain so far, and did it make this list?
How long until the starting zones settle down and the corpse piles go away?

sources.label: Blizzard, WoW: Forever Hotfixes, November 6, 2026

items.title: Blizzard Drops Classic Power Budgets
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, Development Notes
items.synopsis: Blizzard's final pre-launch notes admit Classic power budgets were holding Forever back, and the first live tuning pass is coming Tuesday.
points: Blizzard saying holding to Classic power budgets meant every new element came at the expense of something else
some iconic abilities left feeling lackluster because of it
damage raised on classes across the game, with higher-level creatures given more health to compensate
Blizzard admitting it was "likely hasty" in reaching for Burning Crusade or Wrath-era solutions
the goal not perfect numerical equality, but every class feeling valuable to the group it joins
no big tuning changes until the raids open next month, outside of bugs and serious outliers
Tauren Warriors now correctly starting with +5 Strength over Human Warriors (was +2)
Hunter pets and Warlock Voidwalkers not holding up as tanks, with Classic Era as the target
Affliction finding that always channeling Wrack beats casting their damage-over-time spells

points.text: Enhancement Shamans finding Intellect and Spell Power better than Strength and Attack Power
points.sub: Blizzard: leveling Enhancement players should collect Strength and Attack Power gear from now on

points: class balance changes landing Tuesday, November 10, then on future Tuesdays if necessary
questions: Is moving past Classic power budgets the right call, or does that make Forever just another retail?
What are you playing, and does it feel stronger than it did in the original game?

items.title: Mega-Raids and Proximity Voice
items.category: World of Warcraft: Forever, The Forever Podcast
items.synopsis: The latest WoW: Forever Podcast went all-in on tech, and the big ideas were mega-raids for huge open-world events and proximity voice.
points: Episode 6, All About Tech, hosted by Countdown To Classic with special guest Shobek
Aggrend, Lead Software Engineer Ana Resendez and Principal Software Engineer Frank Williams on the panel
large "mega-raids" floated as the answer for big open-world PvP and roleplay gatherings
proximity voice chat talked about as something they'd like to allow in the game
Discord already wired into both retail and Forever, with account linking and guild chat mirroring
guild leaders choosing whether Discord traffic lands in /guild or a dedicated /discord channel

points.text: in-game voice channels already live, with a push-to-talk bug on Blizzard's Known Issues list
points.sub: push-to-talk instructions can show up by mistake when you join a voice channel

points: no new episode this Thursday, so the show is either skipping a week or running late
questions: Would proximity voice make Forever better, or would it turn Goldshire into a nightmare?
What would a mega-raid open-world PvP night look like for a guild like ours?

items.title: The Community Shows Up
items.synopsis: Launch week was as much about the people as the patch, from a walk to 60 to a campfire drop for watching streams.
points: bigguygrind taking on a walking challenge on stream, all the way to level 60
the starting zones turning into fields of corpses with accelerated spawns, per heyitslissala
the Pouch of Violet Dust Twitch drop running November 4 through November 12 at 4:30 p.m. PST
a purple campfire adding an hour to every camp benefit, two hours total, shared with everyone resting there

points.text: an ephemeral toy, removed from collections when the launch celebration ends in early December
points.sub: link your Twitch account at account.battle.net/connections first

points: Blizzard's Nikki Crenshaw shouting out the RP-PvP community's own newspaper, The Hearthside Herald
the WoW Portal Room Discord pitched as the place to find your next community
Blizzard posting video call backgrounds to tide you over at work until you can log back in
questions: What's the most Forever thing you've seen another player do this week?
Is the community energy this time different from Classic in 2019?

items.title: Gamepads, Taldramir and Forever's Extras
items.synopsis: Blizzard spent launch week explaining the extras: controller play, a Wētā-forged legendary, and how Forever differs from retail.
points: every XInput-compatible controller supported, with Xbox and PlayStation button icons
targeting, casting, looting and menus refined for gamepads, though you still need a keyboard for chat

points.text: gamepad support still in a beta state, with more improvements to come
points.sub: Holly Longdale's "play it wherever" Project Helix comment from last week still hanging over this

points: Taldramir, the Whispering Wood, revealed as Forever's first legendary
Wētā Workshop forging a real-life Taldramir for the Forging Forever video
Classic and Enhanced presets changing presentation only, never which ruleset you play on
Enhanced turning on quest guidance, a one-bag view and transmog by default
the Cooldown Manager and a Damage Meter sitting in Forever's Advanced options
nine new five-player dungeons across levels 13 to 60
the level cap staying at 60, "an expanding game without an expansion of levels"
questions: Has anyone in the guild actually tried leveling on a controller yet?
Is Classic or Enhanced the way you're playing, and why?

items.title: Venomous Abyss Takes a Big Round of Nerfs
items.synopsis: While everyone's in Forever, retail raiders are getting a big round of Venomous Abyss nerfs, Mythic especially.
points: Linxy announcing Venomous Abyss adjustments rolling out over a few days
Ula'tek's Unchecked Rage damage reduced by 61% on all difficulties
Ula'tek's health reduced by 15% on Heroic, with smaller-raid health scaling fixed on Raid Finder, Normal and Heroic
Caustic Waves damage over time cut by 75% on Normal, 61% on Heroic and 89% on Mythic
the Coiled Altar's Malevolent Resonance damage reduced by 60%
Vashnik, the Malignant's Malignance damage reduced by 37% on Mythic
Twin Fangs' Visceral Burst damage reduced by 40% on Mythic
Linxy following up that the Ula'tek changes are already live, ahead of the hotfix post
the Hot Motocross Bunmover mounts getting fixes ahead of next week's maintenance
questions: Does a nerf this big change the plan for anyone still pushing Heroic or Mythic?
Is retail quietly getting easier because everyone's attention is on Forever?

items.title: A Faster, Simpler Xbox App on PC
items.synopsis: Xbox is rebuilding its PC app to launch faster and feel simpler, starting with Insiders.
points: Xbox Insiders getting an updated Xbox PC app that launches up to 60% faster
easier ways to find games, connect with friends and play
the refreshed Xbox web experience reaching more players
cloud gaming app updates on supported TVs and VR headsets
Xbox admitting "we've heard where the experience could be better"
questions: Does anyone actually use the Xbox app on PC, or is it all Battle.net and Steam?
With Forever on a gamepad, does a better Xbox PC app bring WoW any closer to console?
